newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's anti-drug czar says money laundering down.
newsitem.headline: Panama's anti-drug czar says money laundering down.

text.p: Money laundering in Panama is on the decline thanks to government efforts to track offenders, the country's top anti-narcotics official said on Wednesday.
"It's impossible to quantify, but we have seen a decrease in money laundering" in Panama, Gabriel Castro told reporters.
Castro, also the nation's security chief, attributed the drop in part to a special unit which began tracking money laundering last year.
The Financial Analysis Unit, set up in part with U.S. financial and computer assistance, operates like a U.S. Treasury Department unit that targets money laundering.
"Since the financial analysis unit began...we're getting more reports on suspicious financial activities," Castro said.

Anti-drug police track cash transactions of more than $10,000 in financial institutions and free-trade zone businesses in the Atlantic port of Colon. The unit reports to President Ernesto Perez Balladares who recommends whether cases merit prosecution.
